title: Microbiology and infectious agents
audience: a medical student in the preclinical years
purpose: Explain bacterial structure, genetics and laboratory diagnosis, then the major gram-positive and gram-negative bacteria, anaerobes, spirochetes, intracellular bacteria, mycobacteria, DNA and RNA viruses, HIV, hepatitis viruses, fungi and parasites.

blocks.deliverable: Read a Gram stain and culture report.
Distinguish staphylococci and streptococci by their tests.
Match gram-negative organisms to their typical infections.
Week 7 midterm; explain tuberculosis testing and herpesvirus latency.
Interpret a hepatitis B serology panel.
Match fungal and parasitic infections to their exposures.
Submit the project; take an unseen 150 minute final in week 14.

project: Organism profiles and an infection-control plan: summarize ten high-yield pathogens and design the isolation precautions for three scenarios.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
